correctness.rationale: The forced pairs (a,b+3) and (b,a), with b−a≥3, form a matching on the (n−2)(n+1) histories, so subtracting exactly one per pair gives a valid universal upper bound even when other collisions exist. I independently reconstructed the signature table: if the two differences within the second source triple are α,β and its outgoing difference is γ, the insertion replaces γ by (0,−β,−α,α+β+γ) mod 3. Applying this rule to the first defect 0--0 gives all six local signatures and the two generic gaps −d−1 and d−4 in RESULT.md:41–50. The finite output extends by an unchanged periodic tail, and the initial symbol is fixed, so signature equality is exactly word equality. Different histories have the same signature only across the generic families, at a common gap h≥2 and common first defect, giving exactly the commuting pair (a,b+3),(b,a) with b−a=h+1; within either family the history is uniquely determined. This handles legality, end insertions and n=3 (four outputs) as well as general n. The archived checker and output are supplementary, read but not rerun.
residual_risks: The finite exhaustive checker was inspected, not independently executed; the universal result instead follows from the reconstructed symbolic classification.
